'''Shawne DeAndre Merriman'''<ref name="ProFootballReference.com">{{Cite web |title=Shawne Merriman Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/MerrSh99.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230315195831/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/MerrSh99.htm |archive-date=March 15, 2023 |access-date=2023-12-29 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> (born May 25, 1984), nicknamed "'''Lights Out'''", is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Maryland Terrapins football|Maryland Terrapins]] and was selected 12th overall by the [[San Diego Chargers]] in the [[2005 NFL draft]]. He earned [[NFL Defensive Rookie of the Year]] honors in his first season and recorded {{fract|39|1|2}} [[quarterback sack]]s in his first three seasons, also making three [[Pro Bowl]]s as well as two [[All-Pro]] selections. He was hampered by injuries his next three seasons, and the Chargers waived Merriman midseason in 2010. He was picked up through [[waivers (American football)|waivers]] by the [[Buffalo Bills]] that season, but he only played minimally with the Bills due to continued injuries. He was released by the Bills before the 2012 season however, they re-signed him midseason. He retired at the end of the 2012 season.

'''Shawn Wooden''' (born October 23, 1973) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Safety (gridiron football position)|safety]] for nine seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) with the [[Miami Dolphins]] and the [[Chicago Bears]].  He played [[college football]] for the [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish football|Notre Dame Fighting Irish]] and was selected in the sixth round by [[Jimmy Johnson (American football coach)|Jimmy Johnson]], the then-coach of the [[Miami Dolphins]]. Wooden played for the Dolphins for four seasons and then signed a free agent contract with the [[Chicago Bears]] in the 2000 football season.  After one year with the Bears, he returned to the [[Miami Dolphins]] for the remainder of his career. He is currently a financial advisor with Wooden Wealth Strategies.<ref name=wws>{{cite web|title=Former NFL Star Shawn Wooden Joins Florida Firm to Build Out Sports, Entertainment Division|url=https://www.wealthmanagement.com/people/former-nfl-star-shawn-wooden-joins-florida-firm-build-out-sports-entertainment-division|website=Wooden Wealth Strategies|date=27 January 2020 |accessdate=28 February 2021|ref=wws}}</ref>

'''Shawn A. Mayer''' (born March 4, 1979) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] [[defensive back]], and currently a player development coach at [[Rutgers University]].

Originally signed as an undrafted free agent by the [[New England Patriots]] in 2003, Mayer played in 9 games that season, compiling 15 [[Tackle (football move)|tackle]]s, including one in [[Super Bowl XXXVIII]].<ref>{{cite magazine|title=Boxscore|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/football/nfl/boxscores/2004/02/01/1077_boxscore.html|accessdate=December 8, 2006|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=February 1, 2004|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20040604074936/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/football/nfl/boxscores/2004/02/01/1077_boxscore.html|archivedate=June 4, 2004}}</ref> That one Super Bowl tackle remarkably was of [[Carolina Panthers]] wide receiver Ricky Proehl, who attended the same Hillsborough High School as Mayer. He would appear in only 3 games in 2004, and in February 2005 he signed as a free agent with the [[Atlanta Falcons]] who then allocated him to [[NFL Europe]]. Mayer excelled as a member of the [[Hamburg Sea Devils (NFL Europe)|Hamburg Sea Devils]], matching the NFL Europe record for [[interception]]s in a game (3),<ref>{{cite web|title=Records|url=http://nfleurope.com:80/records/individual/sacks|website=[[NFL Europe]]|accessdate=December 8, 2006|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20070810220804/http://nfleurope.com/records/individual/sacks|archivedate=August 10, 2007|url-status=live}}</ref> setting team records for interceptions in a season (5) and in a game (3)<ref>{{cite web|title=Team Records|url=http://www.nfleurope.com/teams/records/HAM|website=NFL Europe|accessdate=December 8, 2006|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20061115150939/http://www.nfleurope.com/teams/records/HAM|archivedate=November 15, 2006}}</ref> and earning All-NFL Europe honors. He would return to play for Hamburg during the 2006 season, this time allocated by the Cleveland Browns.<ref>{{cite web|title=Shawn Mayer - Cleveland Browns|url=http://www2.sportsnet.ca/football/nfl/players/Shawn_Mayer|website=[[Sportsnet]]|accessdate=December 8, 2006|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20071006024139/http://www2.sportsnet.ca/football/nfl/players/Shawn_Mayer|archivedate=October 6, 2007|date=2007}}</ref>

Mayer started 23 games while at [[Penn State University]] and finished his career with 252 tackles, 5 interceptions, 1.5 [[Quarterback sack|sack]]s and 8 tackles for loss. He earned a [[Bachelor of Science]] in Administration of Justice from [[Penn State University]] in 2003.

He grew up in [[Hillsborough Township, New Jersey]]<ref>{{cite news|url=http://nl.newsbank.com/nl-search/we/Archives?p_product=PI&s_site=philly&p_multi=PI&p_theme=realcities&p_action=search&p_maxdocs=200&p_topdoc=1&p_text_direct-0=0EB73613D891A626&p_field_direct-0=document_id&p_perpage=10&p_sort=YMD_date:D&s_trackval=GooglePM|title=LIONS SAFETY MAYER INJURED, WILL MISS SEASON|work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]|date=August 15, 2000|access-date=March 30, 2008|quote=Safety Shawn Mayer, who had figured heavily in Penn State's plans this year, will miss the football season because of a knee injury suffered in practice. ... The 6-foot, 197-pounder from Hillsborough, N.J., played in every game last season.}}</ref> and was twice-named a ''[[USA Today]]'' [[All-America]]n and New Jersey SuperPrep following his junior and senior seasons at [[Hillsborough High School (New Jersey)|Hillsborough High School]] where he also excelled in [[track and field]].

He played in 48 games for the Packers over six seasons, recording 11 sacks and 1 [[interception]].<ref name="PFR"/> He became an immediate starter his rookie year after injuries to other Packers' players.<ref name="EGLE"/> His only interception occurred in a 1990 game against the [[Minnesota Vikings]]; he tipped the ball, caught it and then returned it for a touchdown.<ref>{{Cite news | url = https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-oshkosh-northwestern-pack-defense-do/134729065/ | newspaper = [[The Oshkosh Northwestern]] | date = October 29, 1990 | access-date = November 6, 2023 | type = clipping | via = [[Newspapers.com]] | title = Pack defense does the job | agency = [[Associated Press]] | page = 17 | archive-date = November 6, 2023 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20231106180230/https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-oshkosh-northwestern-pack-defense-do/134729065/ | url-status = live }}</ref> Patterson retired after the [[1993 NFL season]] due to bad knees.
